papers.title: RGD Mutation of the Heparin Binding II Fragment of Fibronectin for Guiding Mesenchymal Stem Cell Behavior on Titanium Surfaces.
papers.abstract: Installing bioactivity on metallic biomaterials by mimicking the extracellular matrix (ECM) is crucial for stimulating specific cellular responses to ultimately promote tissue regeneration. Fibronectin is an ECM protein commonly used for biomaterial functionalization. The use of fibronectin recombinant fragments is an attractive alternate to the use of full-length fibronectin because of the relatively low cost and facility of purification. However, it is necessary to combine more than one fragment, for example, the cell attachment site and the heparin binding II (HBII), either mixed or in one molecule, to obtain complete activity. In the present study, we proposed to install adhesion capacity to the HBII fragment by an RGD gain-of-function DNA mutation, retaining its cell differentiation capacity and thereby producing a small and very active protein fragment. The novel molecule, covalently immobilized onto titanium surfaces, maintained the growth factor-binding capacity and stimulated cell spreading, osteoblastic cell differentiation, and mineralization of human mesenchymal stem cells compared to the HBII native protein. These results highlight the potential capacity of gain-of-function DNA mutations in the design of novel molecules for the improvement of osseointegration properties of metallic implant surfaces.

summary_zh.motivation: 在金属植入物表面通过ECM模拟实现生物活性修饰，以促进组织再生。
summary_zh.method: 通过RGD获得功能DNA突变在纤连蛋白HBII片段上引入粘附能力，并固定在钛表面。
summary_zh.result: 突变蛋白维持生长因子结合能力，促进人间充质干细胞铺展、成骨分化和矿化。
summary_zh.validation: 体外细胞实验验证蛋白活性与成骨分化效果。

summary_en.motivation: To enhance bioactivity of metallic implants by mimicking extracellular matrix through engineered protein fragments.
summary_en.method: A gain-of-function RGD mutation was introduced into the heparin binding II fragment of fibronectin, and the novel protein was covalently immobilized onto titanium surfaces.
summary_en.result: The mutated fragment retained growth factor binding and enhanced mesenchymal stem cell spreading, osteoblastic differentiation, and mineralization compared to native HBII.
summary_en.validation: In vitro cell culture assays evaluated adhesion, differentiation, and mineralization on functionalized titanium surfaces.
